questions.q: A large heating and air conditioning company provides each employee with a small computing device that the employees use to track work and accept payments. Which term refers specifically to this type of device?
questions.explanation: Handheld = small, portable, single-purpose work device. Peripheral attaches to another computer. Microcomputer = PC. Minicomputer = mid-range server.

questions.q: What is the major function of a computer operating system?
questions.explanation: OS manages all computer resources (CPU, memory, storage, devices). Application/data/network management are sub-functions under the resource umbrella.
questions.mnemonic: Broader scope wins. OS = resource manager. Anything more specific is a trap.

questions.q: Within a productivity suite, which method of selecting static data from one application and copying it to another application requires the use of temporary memory?
questions.explanation: Copy/paste uses the clipboard (temporary memory). Embedding inserts an object. Linking creates a live reference.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a universal serial bus (USB) on a laptop or desktop computer?
choices: It allows the computer to connect to peripheral devices.
It provides a wired ethernet connection to the network.
It allows for universal data transmission to various types of wireless networks.
It serves as an internal transmission bus between components within the computer.
questions.explanation: USB = Universal Serial Bus, designed to connect external peripherals (mouse, keyboard, drives, etc).

questions.q: Which category of software includes programs such as word processors and PDF document readers?
questions.explanation: Application software = end-user productivity tools (Word, Acrobat). System software = OS. Utility software = system maintenance (antivirus, defrag).

questions.q: What is the defining characteristic of a part of a system that is considered a point of failure?
choices: It is a part of the system that has failed.
It causes a security risk if it fails.
It is prone to frequent failure.
It causes everything to stop if it fails.
questions.explanation: Single point of failure = if it goes down, the whole system stops. Defines criticality, not failure rate or security.

questions.q: What are the basic components, in addition to computers, that are required for a local network to function?
choices: Internet connection, a network operating system, and a network administrator
Internet connection, a network interface controller, and a cabling system
Ethernet cards, a common protocol, ethernet cables, and a hub
Ethernet cards, a modem, a router, and a network database
questions.explanation: LAN basics = NIC (ethernet card) + protocol (TCP/IP) + cables + hub/switch. Modem and router are WAN/internet, not LAN.
questions.mnemonic: LAN = NIC + Protocol + Cable + Hub. Modem or DB in the answer = TRAP.

questions.q: Which type of device is an ethernet card?
questions.explanation: Ethernet card = NIC. The interface that lets a computer plug into a network.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a MAC address?
choices: To uniquely identify an email client
To uniquely identify a computer motherboard
To uniquely identify a computer on a network
To uniquely identify an internet URL
questions.explanation: MAC (Media Access Control) address = hardware identifier for a device on a network. Burned into the NIC.

questions.q: Which topology implements a network where if the central hub fails, all nodes attached to the hub will also fail?
questions.explanation: Star = all nodes connect to a central hub. Hub dies, network dies. Mesh has redundancy. Bus uses a shared backbone. Ring is circular.

questions.q: Many websites keep track of a user's actions and information. They store much of this information on the user's computer in a private folder on the hard drive. What are these very small files called?
questions.explanation: Cookies = small files stored locally that track session/user data.

questions.q: Every device on the internet has a unique numerical label that identifies it. With so many devices requiring an internet address, a new protocol has been developed that can provide unique identifiers to over 280 trillion devices. What is the designation of this new protocol?
questions.explanation: IPv6 expanded address space from IPv4's 4.3 billion to 340 undecillion addresses. UDP/TCP = transport. HTTP = application.

questions.q: A small online retailer has grown rapidly over the past year, and now during times of high activity, the retailer's web server is nearly at capacity. The retailer anticipates continued rapid growth but is concerned that this growth may stall if the economy goes into recession. What is an appropriate strategic planning decision for this retailer to make in order to ensure adequate server capacity?
choices: Install a load balancer on the server
Use a cloud web hosting service
questions.explanation: Cloud hosting = elastic capacity, pay only for what you use. Load balancer DISTRIBUTES existing capacity, doesn't add it. Clustered servers require buying hardware that may go unused.
questions.mnemonic: Uncertain demand + capacity worry = CLOUD. Load balancer doesn't add capacity, it shares it.

questions.q: Which communication technology has a range of approximately 30 feet and allows smartphones, tablets, and handheld product scanner devices to communicate with a network?
questions.explanation: Bluetooth = ~30 ft personal-area network. Wi-Fi = 100-300 ft. Cellular = miles. GPS = receive-only positioning.

questions.q: Endothon Company buys cabinet hardware from one manufacturer. Due to limited storage space for inventory, Endothon has partnered with the manufacturer to ship hardware just when it is needed. Which component of the IT supply chain could the company set up to efficiently communicate what it needs each week?
choices: An extranet that provides the manufacturer access to data at Endothon
An intranet at Endothon that the manufacturer can access
An intranet at the manufacturer that Endothon can access
An extranet that provides Endothon access to data from the manufacturer
questions.explanation: Endothon needs to push 'what we need' data to the manufacturer = extending Endothon's network outward. That's an extranet from Endothon. Intranets are internal-only by definition.
questions.mnemonic: Give partner access to OUR data = extranet from us. Intranet = internal only.

questions.q: A local drafting firm has a secured local area network that uses Ethernet cables to connect to client computers. After ensuring that the computer is connected to the network, what must a user provide in order to be authenticated?
questions.explanation: Authentication = proving identity (password). MAC address identifies the device, not the user. Encryption keys protect data in transit, not user identity.
questions.mnemonic: MAC = device identity. Password = user authentication. Don't confuse them.

questions.q: Computer system administrators protect the organization when they require strong passwords to connect to the server, enact policies for safe internet browsing, and install malware-protection software to keep unwanted users and viruses out. Which term is used to describe this set of practices?
questions.explanation: Network security = the umbrella term covering passwords, browsing policies, and malware protection at the network level.

questions.q: What is it called when an organization implements security procedures to protect the hardware, network, and software from intrusion?
questions.explanation: System-level security = protecting the system itself (hardware, network, software). Data-level = protecting the data. Access/user-level = controlling who can do what.

questions.q: How does a Gantt chart facilitate project management?
choices: It graphically shows the organization of a project team.
It maps the flow of communication and decisions for a project
It helps calculate the projected and actual costs of a project.
It identifies and sequences the tasks of a project.
questions.explanation: Gantt = horizontal timeline of tasks across time. Identifies and sequences. Communication flows are flowcharts/RACI. Org charts show team structure.
questions.mnemonic: Gantt = TASKS + TIME. Anything about communication = wrong answer.

questions.q: What is the title of the person in the organization who is directly responsible for the setup and operation of the organization's networks, including hardware and software?
questions.explanation: Network administrator = day-to-day operations. Architect = long-term design. Engineer = builds from architect's design.

questions.q: On a day-to-day basis, what is the major focus and responsibility of a chief technology officer?
choices: Keeping the IT development projects on schedule
Managing the IT group and designing the IT architecture
Interfacing with the IT users and setting end-user policies
Ensuring that the IT infrastructure is up to date
questions.explanation: CTO = manages IT group + designs architecture. Project schedule = PM. End-user policies = CIO/CISO. Infrastructure currency = ops manager.

questions.q: What is the title of the person within an IT department whose responsibility is to set policies for passwords, create rules for backup and recovery, and facilitate the protection of the data center and computers with the data and information?
questions.explanation: CISO = security policies (passwords, backups, data center protection). CTO = tech architecture, NOT security. 'Chief cybersecurity officer' isn't a standard C-suite title.
questions.mnemonic: CIS-O: 'Oh shit we got hacked' = the security person's problem.

questions.q: The IT department of a company has been asked to provide systems for financial and investment management. Which business department has the greatest need for this type of system?
questions.explanation: Financial/investment management = Accounting's job. Operations = production. Sales/Marketing = revenue generation.

questions.q: When using extract, transform, and load (ETL), what is done during the 'transform' step?
choices: The data are given context and relevance.
The database schema is designed and created.
The data are normalized and structured.
The database is queried for relevant data.
questions.explanation: ETL transform = normalize + structure (clean format, deduplicate, conform types). Schema design happens before ETL. Querying is post-load.

questions.q: What is the key characteristic that differentiates a datamart from a data warehouse?
choices: A datamart is smaller and more specialized in its focus than a data warehouse.
A datamart is a cloud-based service while a data warehouse requires a dedicated server.
A datamart uses centralized data storage while a data warehouse is decentralized.
A datamart allows a broader set of data structures than a data warehouse.
questions.explanation: Datamart = a focused subset of a data warehouse, often built for one department. Smaller and more specialized.

questions.q: A marketing employee is tasked with mailing discount coupons to the company's top 100 customers by sales volume. The marketing employee only has lists of customers' names, customers' addresses, and the sales generated by each customer. Which process should this employee use to ensure coupons are mailed to the correct customers?
questions.explanation: Data mining = analyzing existing data to extract patterns/insights (like top 100 by sales). Warehousing = storage. Structuring = organization.

questions.q: What is the velocity of big data?
choices: The speed of data produced in a given time
The rate at which the data in a data set become decayed
The frequency with which the data set must be updated
The processing speed of the database servers
questions.explanation: 4 V's of big data: Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity. Velocity = SPEED of production. Frequency of updates and processing speed are TRAPS.
questions.mnemonic: Vince's Vintage Vespa Veered: Volume (lots), Veracity (trust), Velocity (speed), Variety (mixed). Speed = Velocity.

questions.q: Which term is used to refer to data that come from many different sources in various structures?
questions.explanation: Disparate data = many sources, various structures. Unstructured = no defined format (different concept). Semistructured = tags/markers but no rigid schema.
questions.mnemonic: DISPARATE = DIFFERENT sources. Unstructured is about FORMAT, not source count.

questions.q: What are scrubbed data?
choices: Data that have been validated for accuracy
Data that have been eliminated because they are inconsistent
Data that are organized into database tables
Data that have been deleted for privacy reasons
questions.explanation: Scrubbed = cleaned/validated for accuracy. Like scrubbing a pan: you clean it, you don't throw it away.
questions.mnemonic: Scrub the pan = clean it, don't throw it out. Scrubbed data = validated, not deleted.

questions.q: When a company spends money on data management, it uses a metric to measure the benefit of this spending relative to the cost. What is this metric called?
questions.explanation: ROI = the METRIC (a number). Cost-benefit analysis = the PROCESS of comparing. Question asks for metric, so ROI.
questions.mnemonic: Metric = ROI. Process = CBA. The question word 'metric' is the giveaway.

questions.q: One perpetual issue with corporate data is ensuring that the data are accurate and valid. Procedures that apply to end users, managers, and IT personnel are often put in place to ensure good data. What is the term that describes this effort?
questions.explanation: Data governance = the policies and procedures across the org ensuring data quality. MDM is a subset focused on master records.

questions.q: Which level of management gets the most detailed reports directly from the transaction processing system?
questions.explanation: Pyramid: Supervisors get raw TPS detail, Managers get MIS summaries, Executives get EIS dashboards. Closest to transactions = supervisors.
questions.mnemonic: Sammy Sees Specifics, Manny Makes Means, Eddie Eyes Empires. Supervisors = TPS detail.

questions.q: A large online retailer uses a decision support system (DSS) to develop scenarios for the executive team to evaluate. What is the primary source of the data used by this DSS?
questions.explanation: DSS pulls primary data from TPS (the actual transactions). BI synthesizes ALL systems including TPS, but the foundational source for DSS scenarios is TPS.
questions.mnemonic: DSS what-ifs are built on TPS reality. BI is broader, but TPS is the SOURCE.

questions.q: What is a key capability of a decision support system?
choices: It distributes detailed reports to stakeholders for decision-making.
It analyzes data and makes business decisions.
It generates detailed reports of business decisions.
It compiles data from many systems to assist in decision-making.
questions.explanation: DSS COMPILES data from multiple systems to ASSIST decision-makers. It does not make decisions itself.

questions.q: Which strategy can be used to help a company's web page appear on the first page of search results in a browser?
questions.explanation: SEO = optimizing pages to rank organically in search results. SEM/advertising = paid placement. Content marketing = creating content (broader). Analytics = measurement.

questions.q: Which technology enables people without computer programming skills to design and publish their own websites?
questions.explanation: Browser-based web development tools (Wix, Squarespace, etc) = drag-and-drop, no code required.

questions.q: What is the final step in the deployment and use of an app?
choices: Maintain and upgrade the app based on use and user feedback
Track the technical performance and user reviews of the app
Launch the app in the app stores for all applicable platforms
Market the app using focused marketing to reach the desired audience
questions.explanation: Maintain/upgrade = the final ongoing step after launch. Tracking and marketing happen earlier or alongside.

questions.q: Which kind of system should be created to specifically help a company collect and distribute important electronic documents via a computer network as PDF files?
questions.explanation: File-sharing system = built specifically to distribute documents/files over a network. KMS captures collective expertise (broader).

questions.q: Which approach facilitates live communication when a business has employees that are in different locations and telecommute for work?
questions.explanation: Real-time = live, synchronous (video calls, chat). Peer-to-peer = network architecture, not necessarily live. Offline = not live by definition.

questions.q: A company produces a mobile app that provides recipes and cooking tutorials. Which category of app is this?
questions.explanation: Lifestyle = food, fitness, hobbies. Utility = tools (calculator, flashlight). Entertainment = games, video.

questions.q: Which kind of system should be created to help a company organize, create, and distribute the collective experience and expertise of employees?
questions.explanation: KMS = captures + distributes collective employee expertise (the textbook definition). HR = personnel records. CRM = customer interactions.

questions.q: Which file format is suitable to use when sharing a legal contract that requires a digital signature?
questions.explanation: PDF supports digital signatures natively and preserves layout for legal docs. DOCX is editable. HTML/XML are markup.

questions.q: What is a key way that social media marketing has simplified the calculation of return on investment (ROI) in marketing?
choices: By allowing companies to utilize user-generated content as an advertising tool
By allowing companies to track which sales can be connected directly to a specific advertisement
By providing companies with the opportunity to easily solicit customer feedback and interaction
By providing companies with transparent pricing on all advertising offerings
questions.explanation: Direct attribution: track click → sale. Traditional marketing couldn't pin specific sales to specific ads.

questions.q: What is the main reason marketing return on investment (ROI) is easier to measure with social media marketing than with traditional marketing?
choices: Social media surveys provide customer feedback.
User behavior is highly predictable in social media.
Social media users often submit product reviews.
User behavior can be tracked in social media.
questions.explanation: Tracking user behavior (clicks, views, time, conversions) is the technical mechanism that enables ROI measurement.

questions.q: A freelance graphic designer plans to create some marketing images to use in a portfolio as samples for prospective clients. Which action will give the graphic designer initial copyright protection of these marketing images?
choices: Registering the images with a copyright office
Declaring the images to be copyrighted
questions.explanation: Copyright attaches at creation (fixed in tangible form). Registration is optional and only matters for enforcement. Publishing/declaring not required.
questions.mnemonic: Copyright = automatic at creation. Registration is for SUING, not having protection.

questions.q: A start-up software company has designed a program that uses publicly available GPS data to show the location of all city buses and trains in a large metropolitan area. Which legal protection prohibits unethical duplication of this computer program?
questions.explanation: Software code = creative work = copyright. Trademark = brand identifiers. Patent (not in choices) covers inventions/methods.

questions.q: An IT manager for a large organization is working on setting up a system to digitally retain all accounting records and wants to ensure that the system's accounting record retention policies are set in accordance with federal law. Which law should the IT manager become familiar with?
questions.explanation: SOX (2002, post-Enron) = financial record retention and accounting controls for public companies. FOIA = government records. FLSA = labor.
questions.mnemonic: SOX = $$$. Financial records retention law = SOX. FOIA is for GOVERNMENT records, not corporate.

questions.q: An analyst publishes a paper on cybersecurity. In that paper, he includes several pages of a report written by another author, but he does not attribute those pages to the other author. Which type of law prohibits this kind of unethical behavior?
questions.explanation: Plagiarism of published work = copyright violation. Trade secret applies to internal proprietary info that was kept confidential.
questions.mnemonic: Plagiarism = COPYRIGHT (using someone's published work). Trade secret = SECRET internal info someone leaked.

questions.q: What is an example of an Internet of Things (IoT) device?
choices: A motion sensor that turns a light on when movement is detected
A wireless computer keyboard connected to a laptop
A tire-pressure indicator displayed on a car dashboard
A light bulb that can be turned on or off with a smartphone
questions.explanation: IoT = device connected to the internet, controllable remotely. Smart bulb = textbook IoT. Motion sensors and tire-pressure indicators are local sensors, not internet-connected.

questions.q: Where does IoT data collection begin?
questions.explanation: Edge = the IoT sensor/device itself, where physical data is first captured. Then it flows to cloud/database for processing.

questions.q: Which type of technology can be used to monitor every product in a warehouse to enable real-time inventory tracking and updates?
questions.explanation: RFID tags on every product enable real-time scanning and tracking. WAN/OMS are infrastructure, not the tracking tech itself.

questions.q: A homeowner arrives at home in the evening. A timer has turned on an exterior light before her arrival, and the surveillance camera records her walking to the door. She unlocks the door using a mobile app, and a motion sensor turns on an interior light when she enters the house. What is an example of Internet of Things (IoT) technology in this scenario?
questions.explanation: Door lock = controlled by mobile app over the internet = IoT. Timer (exterior light) and motion sensor (interior light) are local automation. Camera is recording, not necessarily networked.

questions.q: How does the healthcare industry use Internet of Things (IoT) devices?
choices: To track ambulance locations and movements
To monitor patients' heart rate and oxygen levels
questions.explanation: Healthcare IoT primary use = wearable/connected devices monitoring patient vitals (heart rate, oxygen, glucose). Ambulance tracking = GPS fleet mgmt. EMR access = software. Research = data analytics.

questions.q: A large automobile maker has added sensors to its assembly line equipment to alert managers to manufacturing anomalies via a mobile application (app) on their smartphones. This Internet of Things (IoT) system connects proprietary manufacturing components. What is the greatest risk created by incorporating this IoT system?
questions.explanation: More connected devices = bigger attack surface. Connecting proprietary manufacturing components to the internet = security risk.
